phase: P06 (batch 2: stock and side effects of checkout completion)
scope: Cart reservations versus inventory reservations (cart reservations never reserve inventory stock)

findings.problem: Stock was deducted after the order transaction committed, through a separate service call. A failure there left a paid order with no stock deducted and no ledger entry, and since P05 an oversell failed at that point with the order already saved. Preorder/backorder rows were only created from a whole-catalogue estimate and only when the variant allowed backorders, so a real shortage on a normal variant left a paid order nobody could fulfil without any record.
findings.change: Stock leaves inside the order transaction: the warehouse row is locked, the available quantity is decremented and an inventory-ledger row (reason order, reference the order) is written. A paid order is never dropped: any shortage at the warehouse becomes a preorder (if the variant allows preorders) or a backorder for staff. A failure anywhere in the transaction rolls the stock back with the order. The post-commit stock call was removed.
findings.verification: CheckoutCompletion integration: baseline stock unchanged after an order and no backorder for a shortage; fixed stock 5 -> 3 with a matching ledger row referencing the order, shortage recorded as a backorder with stock at 0, and an injected failure after deduction leaves stock, orders and ledger untouched.

findings.problem: The purchase analytics event and admin notifications (order created, low stock) were written inside the order transaction and wrapped in try/catch. A database error there still aborts the PostgreSQL transaction (the P02-01 failure mode), so a notification problem could make a paid checkout fail. Failures were also appended to a log file inside the application directory.
findings.change: Analytics and notifications run after the commit; their failures are logged and never affect the order. The on-disk log file write was removed.
findings.verification: Integration case: with analytics writes failing, the order is still created and stock deducted.

tests.updated: complete-checkout-race unit: stock is no longer adjusted after the order transaction
tests.baseline: With the old completion port: the deduction, shortage and analytics cases failed (stock never left in the transaction); the rollback case passed only because nothing was deducted.
tests.database_suites: All E2E and integration suites: 133 tests in 41 files pass
tests.final: 1511 unit tests in 117 files; root/tooling tsc; 7/7 workspace type-checks; API client drift check

follow_ups: Stock is taken from the single resolved warehouse (DEFAULT_STOCK_LOCATION or the first warehouse); multi-warehouse allocation is not implemented.
Backorders created for variants that do not allow backorders should be surfaced to staff (they currently appear in the backorder list only).
